notes.title: Operating philosophy
notes.body: This is a coaching first org. Leaders spend their time coaching: team meetings, 1:1s, reviewing calls and emails, and giving real time feedback. Managers and directors must have serious hands on MDR experience, know how to coach, and have been coached themselves. We deliberately avoid an org bogged down in tools training and low value meetings.

notes.title: Span of control
notes.body: One manager per 8 MDRs to leave real room for coaching. One director per roughly 6 managers, which is about 48 MDRs. Both ratios are the working model and both are open questions for Lynn. At 9,000 meetings a quarter and 13 booked per MDR per month, full capacity is 231 MDRs, which at 8 to 1 is 29 managers and 5 directors.

notes.title: Messaging is owned by Product Marketing
notes.body: Product Marketing already provides messaging and content, so messaging and sequences is owned by PMM

notes.title: The New Hire Trainer stays lean
notes.body: We are not calling this Enablement. It is a New Hire Trainer, deliberately a single role, set up to onboard a new hire through their first month and then hand them to their manager. Ramp is 1 month, not 90 days. If tools and platform training is needed, existing enablement can help.

notes.title: Existing shared functions
notes.body: Operations (rev ops within Richards org) and Content / Messaging already exist on the current team. The Sales Recruiter is not on the team today, so it sits in the hiring list rather than here.

notes.title: Phase 1, 40 hires in Q4
notes.body: Phase 1 is 40 hires in Q4 and it breaks down cleanly: 33 MDRs, 5 managers at one per 8, 1 director, and 1 New Hire Trainer. Teams are seeded at 7 and 6 so each can grow to 8 without adding a manager. The Sales Recruiter is a Phase 1 hire too but sits outside the forty because it is not an MDR org seat.

notes.title: Where capacity lands
notes.body: Today capacity is 107 MDRs, which is 37 internal plus the 70 outsourced live as of 9/8. Once the vendor ramp completes in the middle of October that is 187. The 33 Phase 1 MDRs take it to 220 against a full capacity target of 231.

notes.title: Phase 2, replace outsourced with internal
notes.body: Phase 2 swaps the 150 outsourced MDRs for internal headcount and adds no new capacity. No date set.

notes.title: Phase 3, hire to full capacity
notes.body: Phase 3 takes the org to full capacity at 231 MDRs, which is what 9,000 meetings a quarter needs at 13 booked per MDR per month. No date set.

notes.title: AEs are not decided
notes.body: When the AEs move over is not decided. No AE org is modelled here. The 4 leads per day per sales rep implies roughly 36 receiving reps at 9,000 a quarter, but that is a sizing note, not a plan.

roleDefinitions.title: Head of SMB Sales
responsibilities: Owns the entire MDR org, its number of 9,000 meetings per quarter, and the operating model.
Builds and leads the leadership layer, sets the coaching culture, and hires and develops the directors.
Owns the three phase build: Phase 1 hires 50 in Q4, Phase 2 replaces the outsourced team with internal, Phase 3 goes to full capacity.
Owns capacity planning, headcount ramp, targets and comp.
Stays close to the floor and protects the org from meeting and tool bloat.

roleDefinitions.title: Director of MDR
responsibilities: Owns a segment of roughly 6 managers, which is about 48 MDRs, and their share of the demo target.
Coaches the managers, the coach the coach work, runs manager 1:1s, and holds the coaching standard.
Accountable for team demo output, ramp, attrition and quality, and removes blockers.
Must have real MDR and people management experience.

roleDefinitions.title: MDR Manager / Team Lead
responsibilities: Owns a team of 8 MDRs and their meeting number.
Spends the majority of time coaching: a weekly team meeting, weekly 1:1s with every rep, call and email reviews, and real time feedback.
Takes the rep from the New Hire Trainer at the end of month 1 and owns their performance from there.
Must have serious hands on MDR experience, know how to coach, and have been coached.

roleDefinitions.title: MDR
responsibilities: Books 13 meetings per month against target accounts.
Runs outbound across calls, email, and social, books and holds qualified demos, and hands off cleanly to AEs.
Executes the plays and messaging, which come from Product Marketing, and acts on coaching.
Keeps CRM and activity data clean.

roleDefinitions.title: MDR New Hire Trainer
responsibilities: Owns new hire onboarding and ramp certification through the first month, and is accountable for time to productivity.
Hands the rep to their manager at the end of month 1, at which point the rep is expected to carry the full 13 meetings a month.
Deliberately a single role. Not an Enablement function. If tools and platform training is needed, existing enablement can help.

roleDefinitions.title: Operations (sales ops)
responsibilities: Reporting, tooling, data, and comp and quota mechanics.

roleDefinitions.title: Sales Recruiter
responsibilities: Not on the team today. Net new hire. Fills the hiring pipeline at wave velocity across all three phases.

roleDefinitions.title: Product Marketing
responsibilities: Owns messaging, positioning, and content.

goal.line: Goal: 9,000 demos per quarter. Sales reps receiving 4 leads per day.

discussion.title: Assumptions
items: Span of control is 1 manager per 8 MDRs.

Today the internal team runs 37 MDRs across 4 managers, which is about 9 per manager. The internal team is planning to remain remote but part of Lynn's org. As the team loses MDRS, that headcount moves to Austin.
Directors carry roughly 6 managers, which is about 48 MDRs each.
Each MDR books 13 meetings per month. This replaces the old 10 completed demos per month assumption.
The goal is 9,000 meetings per quarter. At 13 booked per MDR per month that is 3,000 a month, which needs 231 MDRs at full capacity.
Show rate is the step to challenge. The model treats the 9,000 as meetings booked and applies no show rate discount.
If the 9,000 has to be completed demos rather than booked, then at a 77 percent show rate, which is the 10 out of 13 the old model implied, full capacity is 300 MDRs rather than 231.
At 8 to 1 that 231 MDR end state needs 29 managers and 5 directors.
Sales reps receive 4 leads per day. At roughly 21 working days that is about 84 a month per rep, so 9,000 a quarter needs roughly 36 receiving reps.
Phase 1 is 40 hires in Q4: 33 MDRs, 5 managers, 1 director and 1 New Hire Trainer.
Phase 1 teams are seeded at 7 and 6 rather than 8 so each team can grow to 8 without adding a manager.
Outsourced is 70 live as of 9/8 and ramps to a total of 150 by the middle of October.
Outsourced headcount counts toward meeting capacity but not toward internal headcount.
New hires ramp in 1 month. They are assumed fully productive at 13 booked meetings from month 2.
The VP of MDR is moving to another role and that seat is not being backfilled. The internal team rolls up to the Head of SMB Sales through the existing director.
The Sales Recruiter is not on the team today. It is in the hiring list, not in the current headcount.
Rounding up at each stage means staged manager and director counts can land one above the end state number. Those absorb as teams fill.
Phase 2 and Phase 3 have no dates yet.
Timing for moving the AEs over is not decided.

discussion.title: Open questions
items: Do you prefer an 8:1 model or a different ratio?
At 8:1 the 231 MDR end state needs 29 managers.
At 10:1 it needs 24 managers, which is 5 fewer leaders but less coaching time per rep.
At 6:1 it needs 39 managers, which is more coaching but a heavier and more expensive layer.
Second question: how many managers should a director carry?
At 6 managers per director, 29 managers needs 5 directors. This is the working model.
At 8 managers per director it needs 4 directors, which is one fewer leader but thinner coach the coach time.
At 4 managers per director it needs 8 directors, which is much closer coaching of managers and three more leaders to pay for.
Both ratios drive the Phase 1 breakdown, the Q1 hiring plan and the cost of the whole build, so they are worth settling first.

discussion.title: What a manager owns
items: A team of 8 MDRs and their meeting number, which is 13 booked per MDR per month.
Coaching cadence: a weekly team meeting, a weekly 1:1 with every rep, call and email reviews every week, and real time feedback on the floor.
Ramp: takes the rep from the New Hire Trainer at the end of month 1 and owns their performance from there. The rep is expected to carry the full 13 from month 2.
Reporting: weekly team number, meetings booked, and rep level performance up to their director.
Hiring: interviews and selects for their own team, and owns the bar on their own team.

discussion.title: What a director owns
items: Roughly 6 managers, which is about 48 MDRs, and their share of the meeting number.
Coaching the coaches: a weekly 1:1 with every manager, sitting in on team meetings and call reviews, and holding the coaching standard.
Ramp: accountable for time to productivity across the segment and for manager readiness ahead of each hiring wave.
Reporting: segment meetings booked, ramp, attrition and forecast up to the Head of SMB Sales.
Performance: manages out and backfills, and owns the bar across the segment.

discussion.title: Hiring needs for Q1
items: This is an estimate tied to the plan, not a commitment. It is the first thing to confirm.
Q1 is Phase 2 territory, which is replacing outsourced MDRs with internal headcount.
Replacing all 150 outsourced in one quarter is not realistic while the 40 Q4 hires are still landing.
Estimate: replace half the outsourced team in Q1, which is 75 internal MDRs.
That needs about 10 more managers at 8 to 1, since 75 divided by 8 is 9.4.
And 2 more directors. Phase 1 leaves us at 9 managers, so 19 managers at 6 per director is 4 directors against the 2 we have.
Q1 estimate is therefore 87 internal hires: 75 MDRs, 10 managers and 2 directors.
On a 1 month ramp those 75 are productive inside the quarter, which is what makes half realistic.
The vendor contract needs to wind down in step with this so we are not paying for both.
If the Q4 forty land slower than planned, drop Q1 to replacing a third of the outsourced team rather than half.
